p.i: His præerat bello strenuus Diomedes.
Qui autem Mycenas incolebant celebrem vrbem,Corinthus. Cleonæ.
Opulentámque Corinthum, bene habitatásque Cleonas,
Orniásque habitabant, Arathyreamq; amabilem,Sicyon.
Et Syciona, vbi Adrastus primùm regnauit:
Quíque Hyperesiam, & excelsam Gonoessam,Hyperesia. Gonoessa.
Pellenámque habitabant, & Ægium incolebant,Pellene.
Et omnem oram illam maritimam, & circa HelicenHelice.
spatiosam,
Horum centum nauibus imperabat rex Agamemnon.
Quíque incolebant cocauam Lacedæmona immensam,Lacedæmonij.
Pharémque, Spartámque, abundantémque columbisSparta. Phara. Messene. Bryfiæ.
Messenem:
Bryfiasq habitabant, & Augias amabiles:Augiæ.
Quíque Amyclas tenebant, Helósque maritimum op-Amyclæ. Helos.
pidum:
Quiq; Laam habitabant, & Oetylon incolebant:Laa. Oetilos.
His ipsius frater præerat Menelaus.
Quíque Pylúmque habitabant, & Arenen amabilem,Pylui. Arene.
Et Thryon Alphai vadum, & bene adificatum Æpy:Thrion. Æpy.
Et Cyparisseentem, & Amphigeniam habitabant,Cyparissus.
Et Pteleon, & Helos, & Dorion,Pteleon. Helos. Dorion.
His præerat Gerenius eques Nestor.
Quiq; habitabant Arcadiá sub Cyllenes monte altum,Arcadia. Cyllene mons.
Prope Æpyti monumentum.Æpytum.
Qui Pheneumq; incolebant, & Orchomenû pecorosumOrchomenon. Ripe.
Ripénque, Straciénque, & altam Enispen,Stratie. Enispe. Tegea mons.
Et Tegeam habitabant, & Mantineam amabilem:Mantinea.
Stymphalúmque tenebant, & Parrhasien habitabant:Stymphalus lacus. Parrhasia mons.
His imperabat Ancaï filius rex Agapenor.
Qui Buprasiúmque, & Elidem nobilem incolebantElis. Buprasium. Hyrmine.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are place-name glosses; transcribed as printed in abbreviated, run-together form. Several words in the margin are partly obscured by print damage and may be imperfect (e.g. "Ferte"/"Pylui" line, "Lacedæmonij", "Sparta"). Greek-derived forms in the text (Æpy, Cyparisseentem) are as printed.
